text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: INC-2009 · high · queue_backlog_exhaustion · us-west1
incident-bot: Summary: request queue > 95% for service=runtime-prod, autoscaler failing to add capacity for 6 minutes, tokenized latency spikes > 2.5s.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Triggered on escalation policy 'runtime-oncall' · Priority: P1 · Sevs: service health degraded · URL: https://pd.example/incidents/INC-2009

arjun: acked on PD · I'm jumping in. seeing large tail in queue length metric (runtime.queue.depth) in grafana: ~28k pending. autoscaler target pods = 120, current pods = 96.

jen: grabbing quick logs from scale-controller. copying snippets:```
2026-03-14T12:01:04Z scale-controller INFO scale_decision target=120 current=96 reason=insufficient_quota
2026-03-14T12:01:08Z kubeapi ERROR nodeseries: rate limit hit when provisioning nodes: quota_exceeded
2026-03-14T12:02:20Z scale-controller WARN backoff applied next_attempt=30s
```

maria: customers hitting 429/503? Quick check: error-aggregation shows 429s rose from 0.1% -> 6.8% in the last 10m. Major corp keys A123 and B987 showing elevated error rates. No SLO breaches yet but spike trending.

arjun: looks like GKE node pool hit regional quota. I can try manual scale to a different node-pool (non-default) to absorb traffic while we sort quota.

jen: can you also lower the max_batch_size for the runtime route to shed token load? small config change might reduce per-request resource usage.

arjun: doing manual partial mitigation:```bash
# provisional: create 4 aux nodes in aux-nodepool-usw1
gcloud compute instances create-from-template aux-node-quick-01 --zone=us-west1-b --machine-type=n1-standard-16 --image-family=cos-stable --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
# add to k8s by joining cluster via instance group (manual-ish)
```
arjun: submitted the create jobs; should be up in ~2-3m if quota allows.

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by arjun at 2026-03-14T12:05:31Z

jen: reducing runtime route batch size from 1024 -> 512 via feature-flag. Applying patch:```yaml
- name: runtime.batch.max_tokens
  value: "512"
```
jen: patch applied to canary subset (10% of traffic). Monitoring.

maria: talking to account execs for A123/B987, sending heads-up that we're mitigating and will follow-up with postmortem.

arjun: aux nodes came up but kubelet is failing join on 2/4 with error 'instance-limit' (cloud quota). 2 nodes joined -> cluster now 100 pods -> still short. Scale-controller logs show repeated "quota_exceeded" from cloud provider.

jen: alternative: route lower-priority customers to degraded-mode (model-quantized variant) to free capacity for enterprise traffic. Is that possible quickly?

arjun: yes. I can flip routing rule to route 20% traffic served by model-xhq -> model-x-lt (quant). Doing canary switch now.```bash
kubectl patch cm routing-config -n runtime --type merge -p '{"data":{"route_model_xhq":"model-x-lt"}}'```
arjun: patch applied.

maria: monitoring error rates and latency: after canary routing and batch reduction, latency p50 -> 420ms, p95 -> 1.2s, 429s down to 3.1%. Still above baseline but improving. Customer A123 reported fewer failures.

incident-bot: auto-escalation timer 10m remaining. Keep thread updated.

kevin: I'm inbound for the next handoff window at 12:30. If we still have quota issues we should open a cloud support case and request temporary quota bump for region us-west1. Also verify any recent terraform changes that might have reduced node quota.

arjun: good call. filing cloud support case now with logs and request id. Case CS-8342 created: request temporary cpu quota increase + 10 nodes for 1 hour.

jen: adding one more short-term mitigation: enable request-drop for long-tail jobs via runtime throttle:```json
{ "throttle": { "max_concurrency": 1200, "drop_policy": "tail_drop" } }
```
jen: applied to non-enterprise routes.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: INC-2009 updated: acknowledged by arjun, responders: jen, maria, kevin.

maria: quick customer impact summary to paste to execs: "Approximately 5-7% of requests across runtime-prod received 429/503 errors between 11:55-12:10 UTC. Enterprise customers A123/B987 experienced elevated errors ~8-12% during peak. Mitigations applied: manual aux nodes (partial), batch size reduced, routing to quantized model for low-priority traffic, throttle enabled. Errors decreased to ~2-3% within 10 minutes."

arjun: logs show scale-controller will attempt additional scaling every 30s; cloud support case pending. I'll keep watching queue depth and pod counts.

kevin: taking over monitoring. if queue depth doesn't drop below 5k in 20m, escalate to oncall-manager and schedule rollback to earlier config. Also prepare rollback plan doc link: https://confluence/revert-plan/INC-2009

arjun: handing off to kevin — leaving notes in incident channel and marking tasks:
- cloud case CS-8342 (waiting)
- manual aux nodes: 2/4 joined
- routing change applied: model-x -> model-x-lt at 20%
- batch cap reduced to 512 (canary 10%)
- throttle for non-enterprise enabled

kevin: I have it. I'll keep PD updated and will escalate if we see regression. monitoring alerts: runtime.queue.depth.alert (threshold=5000) still firing; silenced for 10m while we validate mitigations.

incident-bot: PD alert auto-note: silenced by kevin for 10 minutes.

maria: pinging AEs with mitigation summary and ETA for full remediation (depends on cloud quota).

kevin: next update in 15m or sooner if status changes. taking this to oncall H1.

pagerduty: Incident INC-2009 status: Mitigations in place · Monitoring · Owner: kevin

arjun: thanks all. will be available if kevin needs help.

kevin: thanks, closing active pager handoff. I'll post a follow-up thread once cloud quota case updated or when queue settles. :thumbsup:
